summary: Online research for rev0118 supports the fail-fast design: offline model execution requires pre-downloaded cached model files and explicit offline/local-only controls, safetensors/source locks reduce serialization/provenance risk, and CUDA event timing only becomes evidence on a CUDA device with proper synchronization.

sources.title: Transformers installation/offline mode
sources.observed: Offline Transformers use requires downloaded/cached files ahead of time and can use snapshot_download/local-only flow. Search ref turn816902search4.

sources.title: Transformers v4.47.1 offline mode
sources.observed: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is documented for firewalled/offline Transformers workflows. Search ref turn816902search0.

sources.title: huggingface_hub environment variables
sources.observed: HF_HUB_OFFLINE is the environment-side control for offline hub behavior. Search ref turn816902search1.

sources.title: Safetensors documentation
sources.observed: Safetensors is described as a simple, safe, fast tensor format, replacing pickle-style hazards. Search ref turn816902search6.

sources.title: PyTorch CUDA Event documentation
sources.observed: CUDA events are synchronization markers for monitoring device progress and measuring timing. Search ref turn816902search3.

sources.title: NVIDIA CUDA event elapsed time API
sources.observed: CUDA event elapsed time is reported in milliseconds and is a device-side timing primitive. Search ref turn816902search21.

design_implications: Do not let the current trace lane proceed if the runtime lacks transformers or a complete reviewed snapshot and downloads are disabled.
Record explicit skipped expensive steps when prerequisites fail, so a blocked capsule produces useful receipts without wasting probes.
Keep safetensors/source-lock checks in the prerequisite lane before any public trace evidence can be accepted.
Treat CUDA timing as unavailable unless a real CUDA device and synchronized CUDA events are present.
scope_boundary: This research note is not model evidence; it justifies runtime/offline guard behavior and remaining blocker classification.
